rationale:
The requirement has three obligations. Both constructors must use the supplied language regardless of the filename's extension. They must return root contents. The value must retain that language's fingerprinting rules. The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]` covers all three.

- **Both constructors, extension ignored:** The test builds a `CustomLanguage` whose extension is `custom`. It calls `from_source_with` with the filename `misleading.rs`. It also writes a `misleading.rs` file to a temp directory and calls `from_path_with` with a clone of the language. A Rust outliner picked from the `.rs` extension would not give a single item with span 0..9 and the scheme `custom-v2`, so these assertions would catch it. The test checks both results in one loop.
- **Root contents:** For each result the test asserts `id().selector == ""`, `text() == "a hello z"`, and the first outline item's span is 0..9.
- **Retained fingerprint rules:** For each result the test asserts the fingerprint value is `a hello z` and the scheme is `custom-v2`. It then drops the language, its clone and the `Arc` scheme, and `fingerprint_scheme()` still returns `custom-v2`. So the value keeps its own copy of the scheme and doesn't borrow it from the language. Selecting `part[selected]` gives the expected text and structural hash. The path-loaded and source-supplied selections have equal fingerprints. The root and the selection have different fingerprints. A second language with scheme `custom-v3` gives the same structural hash but a different fingerprint. That shows the scheme is part of the fingerprint.

The requirement's text names no failure cases. `fn[explicit_language_errors_and_invalid_spans_are_not_plain_text_successes]` separately covers explicit-language errors, but it belongs to `requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`. The cited `snapshot` requirement is also exercised by this test: text, outline and scheme stay together in the loaded value. The test doesn't edit a file after loading it. That property is not part of this subject's own obligations.

I found no gap.

text: The caller can supply an `OutlineLang` explicitly when loading a file or
outlining supplied text. These constructors use that language regardless of
the filename's extension and return root contents. The value retains that
An `OutlineContent` retains the source text, outline, and selected language's
fingerprinting scheme describing that same snapshot. Its item spans, selected
text, and structural hashes are derived from those bytes. A cached value keeps
these parts together; later file edits do not change the loaded value.
